title: A route you can walk
concept: An authored isometric pump, handwheel valve and flanged piping assembly gives the viewer a physical route to follow. An elevated copper bypass branches before the valve and rejoins after it, making the changed connectivity visible without turning the story into a dashboard. The equipment lifts away to expose stable port identities; the review step returns to both tie-ins; the final layered drawing preserves original, change and unresolved review together. All diagram data is illustrative, not performed engineering or an approved plant design.
metaphor: A small engineering model on a drafting floor: the viewer walks a pipe route, lifts the equipment, adds a proposed route and marks the joins that require review.
choreography: The physical pump, motor, valve, supports and base route rise from an isometric floor; short flow marks establish inlet and outlet.
Pump and valve lift separately off the line, exposing labelled stable ports and their DesignGraph links.
The route choice either retains the base assembly or builds an elevated copper bypass with visible branches, risers, flanges and additional flow direction.
The base assembly recedes while the proposed route and two tie-in rings become the review focus; unresolved inputs remain explicit.
The equipment settles over layered source drawings, keeping the original route, linked change and pending review visible together.
interaction: In phase 2, Base route shows the valve route alone; Add bypass directly renders an elevated additional route before and after Valve B. This is a proposed possible flow path, not a claim that the valve is closed, flow is balanced or the route is approved.
contributions: Reusable isometric pump, handwheel valve, flange and support primitives with dimensional SVG shading.
A physically traceable proposed bypass with visible tie-in points and motion that remains legible when paused or disabled.
A bilingual phase narrative that separates stable identity, changed calculation paths and unresolved human review.
limitations: Illustrative geometry is not a P&ID standard, routed construction model or calculation result.
The review and outcome phases deliberately retain the proposed bypass even if phase 2 is currently set to Base route, so the authored change-review story remains visible.
No flow split, pressure, dimensions, valve operating state or plant-specific engineering data is supplied or inferred.
Pure Node contract validation is used in production; browser rendering and judging are reserved for the competition host.
